text: Jesus asked for a guest room. He was given a large upper room, "furnished and prepared." Your part is to prepare what's already prepared.
explanation:
Jesus sent two disciples to follow a man carrying a pitcher of water, unusual in a day when women drew the water, and to ask the master of the house for a guest room. The man gave them far more: a large upper room, already furnished. Even our "preparing" is just making ready what God has already prepared.

God promised Israel "houses full of all good things, which you did not fill, hewn-out wells which you did not dig, vineyards and olive trees which you did not plant." Expect to step into blessings you didn't sweat for. Follow those who carry living water, whose lives show the fruit of what they preach, and keep your eyes on the Lord, the Source.

text: Eucharist means "good grace." A crumb of it is enough. Just ask the mother who said even the dogs eat the crumbs.
explanation:
In the upper room, Jesus took bread and gave thanks: eucharisteō, from eu (good) and charis (grace). It's primarily a way to remember Him, like gazing at the photo of someone you love. But Paul also says that failing to discern His body is why many were weak and sick. Discern it rightly, and the reverse happens.

A Gentile mother asked Jesus only for crumbs, and He called it great faith. People spend fortunes on treatment, then despise a small piece of bread that costs nothing because it cost Jesus everything. Many have taken the Lord's Supper daily, like medicine, believing they're getting better, and have recovered from conditions doctors called impossible.

text: "Until now you have asked nothing in My name." Even after teaching them the Lord's Prayer, Jesus showed His disciples a closer way to pray.
explanation:
The Sermon on the Mount was preached on a hill in Galilee to disciples not yet born again. It brought them to the end of themselves and included "Our Father in heaven," a prayer with distance in it. In the upper room on Mount Zion, a higher mountain, Jesus shared church truths in seed form: the coming Spirit, His return, and prayer in His name.

When Jesus prayed, He simply said, "Father." You're seated with Christ in the heavenly places, in the family. Don't pray as though God is far away and you're straining to reach Him. That isn't true, and the Spirit of truth only bears witness to truth. Pray as a son or daughter at home.

text: A tramp and a billionaire lie side by side in the mortuary. Both need a resurrection. Jesus didn't come to make bad people good, but dead people alive.
explanation:
God doesn't grade sins on a curve, as if your small ones look fine beside someone else's big ones. Without Christ, everyone is "dead in trespasses." The good news is that the dead are exactly the people a resurrection is for. You only miss it if you think you're alive.

"But God, who is rich in mercy, because of His great love with which He loved us, even when we were dead… made us alive together with Christ." Mercy isn't for perfect people; there's no room in church for them. However far you've fallen, His love isn't just love. It's great love.

text: "I bestow upon you a kingdom, just as My Father bestowed one upon Me." You're seated with Christ, and kings rule by speaking.
explanation:
In the upper room Jesus told His disciples He was conferring on them kingly authority, as the Father had conferred it on Him. God's first words to man were "Let them have dominion." Those who receive grace and righteousness "reign in life" like kings.

Kings don't chase problems with a stick. They speak. "Death and life are in the power of the tongue." Yet every language is full of casual death: "I'm dying for that cake." It took the devil over nine hundred years to kill Adam; many now talk themselves into decline. Watch your words. Speak life, in Jesus' name.

text: On a dark country road, a car appeared from nowhere and sounded its horn. He was in the wrong lane. When he looked back, the car was gone.
explanation:
One winter night, driving with his family on an unlit road, Joseph Prince followed the reflectors and, without realising, drifted into the lane for oncoming traffic. A car suddenly appeared, honked to warn him, and vanished. He stopped, saw headlights approaching in the distance, and reversed safely into the right lane.

"He who dwells in the secret place of the Most High": the word for dwells means sits. You're seated with Christ, and from there, "no evil shall befall you… for He shall give His angels charge over you." "Some have entertained angels unawares." Thank God for the deliverances you know about, and for the many you never will.

text: Elijah carried the dead boy to the upper room. The Shunammite laid her son in the upper room. Dorcas was laid in an upper room. Eutychus fell from one. All were raised.
explanation:
Scripture keeps returning to the upper room as a place of resurrection. The upper room is also where Jesus opened His heart, instituted the Lord's Supper, and where the Spirit fell at Pentecost. It speaks of the heavenly places where you're seated with Christ, expressed on earth in the local church.

Eutychus, whose name means fortunate, fell asleep during Paul's preaching and fell to his death. Paul went down, embraced him, and he lived. Expect resurrection: sons and daughters who drifted from God coming back, the spiritually asleep waking up, the lost being saved. Nothing is beyond the God who raises the dead.
